signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5841 as the G10 Currency Strength Scorecard establishes AUD as the weekly leader at +1.144% across 4 pairs against CHF as the laggard at -0.576% across 6 pairs. The resulting 1.720% spread triggers a critical bilateral theme signal. Fundamentals heavily support this gap: RBA policy rate at 4.6% vs SNB at 0.00% creates a +460bp nominal carry advantage, while AONIA at 4.60% vs SARON at -0.06% locks in +466bp in OIS carry favoring AUD. The move is reinforced by retail positioning, where retail sits 87% short AUD/CHF, providing a contrarian tailwind as retail fades the dominant trend. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF, supported by carry advantage and bilateral outperformance. Catalyst: Australia PPI release on 29 Oct followed by RBA meeting on 3 Nov. Risk: Broad cross-asset risk-off liquidation driving acute safe-haven bids into CHF, compressing the spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.82, resting below its SMA20 at 157.93 and SMA200 at 158.49 within a range-bound technical box. The 25-delta risk reversal sits at -2.18 (Saxo Bank, 1M tenor, indicative mid), showing an extreme put skew that marks strong institutional demand for USD downside protection despite CFTC Leveraged Funds remaining net short JPY at -25,598 contracts. Meanwhile, the Fed at 4.0% vs BoJ at 1.25% generates a 275bp policy spread, complemented by SOFR at 3.95% vs TONA at 1.23% giving USD a +272bp OIS carry premium. Middle East tensions and Hormuz shipping concerns introduce headline volatility, but 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered intervention concerns; carry sustains the baseline while options markets actively hedge downside tail risk. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, balancing structural carry against aggressive downside options hedging. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI print followed by BoJ Interest Rate Decision on 30 Oct. Risk: BoJ unexpectedly turns hawkish at the press conference, prompting an immediate unwind of crowded JPY short positioning.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1162, positioned entirely below its SMA20 (1.1209), SMA50 (1.1412), and SMA200 (1.1572) within an entrenched technical downtrend. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds heavily net short EUR at -94,138 contracts, placing the pair at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z = -1.72), indicating crowded speculative short exposure. Concurrently, EUR/USD ATM IV sits at 6.5% against HV30 of 4.1%, generating a notable +2.4% vol risk premium that reflects elevated demand for hedging into policy decisions. The Fed at 4.0% vs ECB at 2.65% provides a 135bp policy spread (SOFR vs €STR carry +151bp in USD favor), keeping upside structurally capped while retail sentiment sits at 86% long, creating sharp downside liquidity if support cracks. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; downward trend structure and carry favor USD, though crowded spec shorts warn of squeeze risk. Catalyst: ECB Interest Rate Decision and press conference on 29 Oct. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish hold or guidance, triggering short covering against crowded Leveraged Fund positions.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Technical Breakdown + Real Yield Shift
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3982, breaking below its SMA20 (1.4149) and SMA50 (1.4019) to print a bearish wide-range bar 2.0 times the 10-bar average body, confirming reversal risk against the intermediate uptrend. While the Fed at 4.0% vs BoC at 2.5% maintains a 150bp policy carry advantage (SOFR vs CORRA +171bp favoring USD), the Bank of Canada's recent 25bp hike to 2.50% has shifted rate momentum. In the US, FRED 5Y yield decomposition shows a 5-day nominal decline of -10bp driven by real yields falling -19bp against breakevens rising +9bp as of 26 Oct, softening real-rate support for the dollar. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold CAD net short at -92,789 contracts (pctl 12, z -1.42), leaving the pair vulnerable to continued short covering if technical support at the SMA200 (1.3880) is tested. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD, leaning into intraday technical breakdown and CAD short-covering flow. Catalyst: Canada GDP and US Core PCE releases on 29 Oct. Risk: US Core PCE prints significantly above expectations, reigniting Fed hike pricing and lifting the pair back above 1.4020.
